title: Describe a Careful Online Reading Check

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料，尚待发布前独立审核。

instructions: Prepare briefly, then record your own answer. Aim for 90–120 seconds; this is a suggested target, not a minimum. Use at least six lesson words. To pass review, your answer’s transcript must contain at least 100 words, and the required audio and review evidence must be available. The reference and its audio are short language examples, not full-length demonstrations; create your own answer.
prompt: Describe a fictional online article you want to check. Explain one claim, two things you would compare, and one privacy choice before sharing. Aim to speak for 90–120 seconds and use at least six lesson words.
reference: I would check a community article about a garden event. The headline might give a larger number than the source record, so I would compare it with notes from the organizer. I would also read the caption under the picture and ask who took it. A photograph is useful evidence, but it does not always show the date. If the publication includes an advertisement, I would look for a clear label. Before I forward an image, I would ask whether the people in it have given permission. They may prefer privacy, and I could use a picture without faces. I would explain the result in a short comment rather than make a claim that the evidence cannot support.
